item.title: WordPress wp2shell CVEs get exploits as Microsoft warns of ACR Stealer surge
item.content:encoded:
WordPress Core "wp2shell" RCE flaws get public exploits, patch now — Must Read

Public exploits are now available for the critical WordPress Core “wp2shell” flaws that can enable unauthenticated remote code execution on affected 6.9.x and 7.0.x sites. Administrators should immediately update to WordPress 7.0.2 or 6.9.5, with WAF or REST API blocking only as temporary mitigation.

  • Public proof-of-concept exploits have been released for the critical “wp2shell” remote code execution vulnerabilities affecting WordPress Core.
  • The wp2shell attack chains CVE-2026-63030, a REST API batch-route confusion flaw, with CVE-2026-60137, an SQL injection flaw in the author__not_in parameter of WP_Query.
  • The complete remote code execution chain affects WordPress 6.9.0 through 6.9.4 and WordPress 7.0.0 through 7.0.1, and it has been fixed in WordPress 6.9.5 and 7.0.2.
  • WordPress has enabled forced automatic security updates for supported installations running affected versions and urged site owners to update immediately.
  • Cloudflare deployed WAF protections for both vulnerabilities, while watchTowr said it has seen public exploit code in circulation and the first signs of in-the-wild exploitation.

Microsoft warns of surge in ACR Stealer attacks on customers — Must Read

Microsoft says ACR Stealer attacks are surging against enterprise customers, using ClickFix lures, WebDAV, MSHTA, and obfuscated PowerShell to steal browser credentials, tokens, and business documents. Organizations should restrict risky script/tool execution and web-based delivery paths to reduce exposure.

  • Microsoft observed a surge between late April and mid-June in attacks using ACR Stealer to steal browser-stored passwords, authentication tokens, and sensitive documents from enterprise customers.
  • The threat actor used ClickFix social engineering, WebDAV servers, and the MSHTA utility to deliver the ACR Stealer payload.
  • One common intrusion chain uses a ClickFix lure to run a malicious DLL from a remote WebDAV share with rundll32.exe, followed by obfuscated PowerShell, a bundled Python loader, persistence through a scheduled task, and in-memory payload execution.
  • A second common intrusion chain uses ClickFix to launch MSHTA, retrieve malicious content from the attacker’s server, run an obfuscated PowerShell downloader, and execute an encrypted payload hidden inside a publicly hosted JPEG image.
  • Microsoft recommends defenses including avoiding copied command instructions from websites, filtering or blocking low-reputation and new domains, restricting unnecessary online resources, and using application control rules for tools such as PowerShell, Python, mshta.exe, and rundll32.exe.
